title: Secrets Underground

beats.narrativeText: Restoring power reveals an underground geological survey area previously inaccessible.
The surrounding landscape contains unusual geological features that may explain many earlier observations.
The learner examines rock samples and compares geological layers left behind by the expedition.
beats.trigger: Rock samples examined and layers compared

beats.narrativeText: Interpreting the expedition's survey maps begins to reveal the shape of the surrounding landscape.
The learner must explain their findings using evidence from the samples, layers and maps together.
The unusual geological features are shown to have influenced many of the expedition's earlier decisions.
The learner reflects on how the environment itself shaped the expedition's research.
The learner uncovers the environmental context behind the expedition's research, and several previously unexplained observations now make sense.

activities.title: Examine Rock Samples
activities.storyContext: An underground geological survey area has become accessible for the first time.
activities.instructions: Examine the rock samples the expedition collected and note their properties.
activities.output: Notes on the properties of each rock sample.

activities.title: Compare Geological Layers
activities.storyContext: The surrounding landscape contains unusual geological features.
activities.instructions: Compare the layers visible in the survey area and note anything unusual.

activities.title: Interpret Survey Maps
activities.storyContext: The expedition's survey maps hold clues about the shape of the surrounding landscape.
activities.instructions: Interpret the survey maps to understand the layout of the geological features.
activities.output: An interpretation of the survey maps.

activities.title: Explain Findings Using Evidence
activities.storyContext: The geological features may explain several previously unexplained observations.
activities.instructions: Explain what your findings reveal, using evidence from the samples, layers and maps together.
activities.output: A written explanation supported by combined evidence.

activities.title: Produce a Geological Field Sketch
activities.storyContext: A field sketch would help future Explorers understand the survey area at a glance.
activities.instructions: Produce a geological field sketch of the surrounding area, labelling key features.

activities.title: Studying Landscapes Without Disturbing Them
activities.storyContext: Geologists study landscapes carefully, without damaging them.
activities.instructions: Find out how geologists study landscapes without disturbing them.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: How did the landscape around the station affect the expedition's earlier decisions?

discussionPoints: What surprised you about the landscape around the station?
How did the geology help explain earlier expedition decisions?
parentGuide.preparation: No special preparation required; real rocks or stones can be used to practise comparing properties if available.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for findings explained using evidence from the samples, layers and maps together, not just one source.

completionCriteria: Rock samples examined, geological layers compared, and findings explained using evidence.
